theory: A paper search returns leads; a fetched version becomes an immutable identified record whose source bytes can be inspected and cited. Statement inventory is separate from assumption admission, so reading a paper never automatically widens the proof trust base.
instead_of: A freeform citation string or a current-title cache would be simpler, but would not identify what was actually fetched, read, or assumed.

absorption.rationale: Another source-bundle shape can extend admission; another repository of papers needs a less arXiv-specific identity contract.

world_mapping.rationale: Search leads, fetched versions, read sources, citations and admitted assumptions remain distinct facts.

abstraction.rationale: Acquisition is separated from immutable storage and inventory; injected transport supports independent testing.

justification.rationale: The client explains why search results are not automatically admitted to the library.

honest_limits.rationale: Archive integrity is enforceable, but lexical statement inventory and source identity cannot establish a paper claim is true.

rehearsals.requirement: Accept another bounded archive encoding of an arXiv version
rehearsals.why: Extend archive admission while retaining path, type and quota checks.

rehearsals.requirement: Use DOI-only publications with mutable publisher source revisions
rehearsals.why: Paper identity and endpoints are currently arXiv-version shaped.
Inventory already translates source environment structure into named Statement values.
